items.title: Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm
items.text: Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf. A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms (and 0.4 ms for @jack's "setting up my twttr" 😁). X is the global town square, and the medium is the message. Being able to preview what things will look like before posting is great for both humans and agents. Rendering with xeet is is 100x-1000x faster than booting up a browser and taking a screenshot, yet it's just as accurate. items.text: "When you ask Claude to create something, it's operating in a fresh context where it thinks: Oh my God, the user asked me to make an app. I'm going to invent the most brilliant visual style." From @nateparrott at Anthropic on how to get Claude to avoid the same designs: "It's going to be serif text, an off-white background, orange, and these bars on the edges of the cards. Because in Claude's mind, it's only ever done this once, so it thinks this is totally original. So in our Claude Design prompt, we tell Claude, 'For this particular model, you tend to overly bias toward these two fonts and colors. So don't use them unless the user asks you to.'
